resolved.title: 连接
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Concatenation[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

In Python math works with words as well as numbers.

So not only can we add integers and floats, but also strings, using something called [b]concatenation[/b], which can be done on any two strings. Like this:
[code format="py" codeId="3888"]print("Spam" + 'eggs')[/code]
And it even works with numbers! Strings containing numbers are still added as strings rather than integers. Like this: 
[code format="py" codeId="3889"]print("2" + "2")[/code]
[note]But don’t try to add a string to a number! Even though they might look similar, they are two different entities, so doing this will break the code and produce an error.[/note]

resolved.title: 字符串运算
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]String Operations[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

You may not be able to add strings to integers, but you can multiply by them!

Multiplying a string by an integer, produces a repeated version of the original string. Like this:[code format="py" codeId="3891"]print("spam" * 3)

print(4 * '2')[/code]
[note]But don’t try to multiply a string by another string. This will just generate an error. The same will happen if you try to multiply a string by a float, even if the float is a number.[/note]
